issues.legal_issue: A pleading may be amended after the limitation period has expired when the amendment corrects a defect without introducing a new case or changing the relief sought, and does not cause injustice that cannot be compensated.
material_facts: A suit seeking a declaration of entitlement to possession was brought after an obstruction-removal application was dismissed.
The original pleading relied on an earlier possession decree but did not state the particular facts supporting the plaintiff’s title against the obstructing defendant.
The proposed amendment supplied particulars of the asserted title and explained the relationship between the defendant and the property; it did not change the relief sought.
The defendant had objected to the lack of particulars before the amendment was requested, and the Court found that the amendment did not take him by surprise or require him to meet a new claim.
The amendment request was made after the limitation period for the suit had expired, and the appellate court allowed it subject to terms including costs.
issues.conclusion: The amendment was properly allowed notwithstanding that the limitation period had expired, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court has discretion to allow amendments necessary to determine the real controversy, provided they do not work injustice to the other side. Expiry of limitation is a relevant factor, but does not remove the court’s power to allow an amendment. An amendment should generally be refused where it sets up a fresh time-barred claim that deprives the other party of a defence that cannot be compensated by costs. The Court applied Charan Das v. Amir Khan, followed L. J. Leach & Co. v. Jardine Skinner & Co., and approved Batchelor J.’s observations in Kisandas Rupchand v. Rachappa Vithoba. The suit arose under Order XXI, rule 103, following proceedings under rules 97 and 99 of the Code.

rule.if: pleading_amendment_request and limitation_period_expired and amendment_supplies_missing_particulars and amendment_preserves_claim and amendment_preserves_relief and opponent_not_surprised and prejudice_compensable_by_costs

predicates.pleading_amendment_request: A party requested amendment of a pleading in a civil suit.
predicates.limitation_period_expired: The limitation period for bringing the relevant suit had expired before the amendment was requested.
predicates.amendment_supplies_missing_particulars: The proposed amendment supplied particulars missing from the original pleading about the factual basis of the claim.
predicates.amendment_preserves_claim: The proposed amendment did not introduce a new case or a fresh claim.
predicates.amendment_preserves_relief: The proposed amendment did not change the nature of the relief sought.
predicates.opponent_not_surprised: The opposing party was not taken by surprise by the proposed amendment and did not have to meet a new claim.
predicates.prejudice_compensable_by_costs: Any disadvantage caused to the opposing party could be addressed by costs rather than depriving that party of an uncompensable defence.

issues.definition: When a party requests amendment of a pleading after limitation has expired, the amendment may be allowed if it supplies missing particulars while preserving the claim and relief, does not surprise the opponent, and causes no prejudice that cannot be compensated by costs.
